text:
J.T. Compher has 3 goals and 4 assists in 15 games for Detroit, on a team playing without Dylan Larkin, who has refused to play until he is traded. He scored on a breakaway against Florida on Nov. 12, in the game the Red Wings lost after leading 4-1; ClutchPoints and Yahoo Sports carried his blunt reaction afterward.

The scoring is a little ahead of his chances. He has 3 goals on 1.68 expected goals and a 15% shooting percentage. The bigger issue is five-on-five: Detroit gets only 43% of the expected goals with him on, 8.5 points worse than when he sits.

That is a problem for a middle-six center. Last season Evolving-Hockey had most of his value coming from even-strength offense and penalties drawn, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking showed a transition player: 53% of his shots off the rush, carry-ins on 54% of his entries. A Stanley Cup winner with Colorado, he knows what a contender's middle-six center looks like. Watch whether Detroit's chances against settle down with him on the ice.
headline: Scoring more than his chances
